That is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>n</mi><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{np(1 - p)}</annotation></semantics></math>, the standard deviation of the count of seeds that sprout. items.q: Assuming the company's figure is correct, find the probability that 80% or fewer of the 200 seeds sprout.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.80</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\hat{p} \ge 0.80)</annotation></semantics></math>, the area above 0.80. "80% or fewer" is the area below.

That uses 0.80 in the standard deviation. The sampling distribution is built from the true <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.85</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = 0.85</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>0.85</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{0.85(0.15)/200}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That uses a standard deviation of 0.0357, which is <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>0.85</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>100</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{0.85(0.15)/100}</annotation></semantics></math>: a sample size of 100. With 200 seeds, <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>0.85</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{0.85(0.15)/200}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.0252</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.0252</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Type the expression for the z-score of <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p} = 0.80</annotation></semantics></math> in this sampling distribution, with the values substituted (as you would show it on the exam).

mistakes.why: The standard deviation of <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{p}</annotation></semantics></math> uses the true <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.85</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = 0.85</annotation></semantics></math>, not the value 0.80 you are standardizing.

The standard deviation needs a square root: <math class="stat-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>0.85</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>200</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{0.85(0.15)/200}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Subtract in the order value minus mean, so a value below the mean gets a negative z-score.
